payload.statement:
# Problem: Council review of Chapter 4, Ancestries & Cultures (quarto-book/chapters/04-ancestries-cultures.qmd)

You are the hol-rulebook council. Audit this chapter as a publishable unit of the Heroes of Legend
TTRPG rulebook and produce a disposition plan. Do NOT fix anything; file findings only.

## Scope
The registered source `04-ancestries-cultures` (the chapter's .qmd). Cross-check against the rest of the
book where a claim is canon-determined (skill roster ch07, core resolution/boon-bane ch06, combat/conditions
ch13, disciplines ch08, class abilities ch05, talents ch09, reference sheets ch22). The chapter covers: the
four ancestries (Human/Elf/Dwarf/Halfling) with their Discipline + trait, the culture tables (skill bonus +
Disciplines per culture), and the Ancestry Gifts (four tables, Novice/Adept/Master ladder).

## Locked conventions the chapter must satisfy (cite the violated convention in every finding)
- **Damage budget = FLAT numbers, on the table, no dice.** Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21
  (Weak/Standard/Strong). "The table is the law." Every damaging/healing number must be a budget row, an
  explicit Basic-card floor, or a damage-TIER bump.
- **ZERO flat +N damage riders (weapons rework, 2026-08-19, book-wide).** Any "deals +N damage (flat)",
  "+N damage", "gains +N damage" is DEAD anywhere in the book, including magic items, talents, and ancestry
  gifts. The canonical way to raise damage is "+1 damage tier (one row up on the damage budget)".
- **Boon/Bane definition (ch06):** Boon = roll 4d6 keep the highest three; Bane = roll 4d6 keep the lowest
  three. A Boon is NOT "an extra d6".
- **Ancestry gifts:** 4-5 per ancestry, mostly Novice/Adept, Master rare. Ceiling rule: no gift out-performs a
  class ability at the same tier. Cost is the flat card price (2/4/8 DP) regardless of class.
- **Ladder discipline:** Novice = 1 disc (or none), Adept = EXACTLY 2, Master = EXACTLY 3 (max 3 ever).
- **Style law: ZERO em-dashes** in prose. No damage dice (only sanctioned 3d6 one-rolls / boon-bane 4d6).
- **No stale vocabulary** (GM -> DA, retired conditions, retired damage types). Skill names must match the
  ch07 roster exactly. Cross-references (@sec-*) must resolve.

## Findings format (one finding per member this round)
Each finding must be decision-oriented: name the broken value with [04-ancestries-cultures:LINE], the
expected/correct value, the violated convention, and the minimal fix. Cite cross-chapter canon lines where the
expected value is canon-determined. Severity is implicit in the fix size. Do NOT invent defects to look
thorough; a chapter with few real problems is a good outcome.

payload.argument: Chapter 4 does not hold as a publishable unit: it contains two direct violations of locked book conventions plus one structural gap, each with a precise fix. Defect 1 [04-ancestries-cultures:181]: the Forge-Trained gift grants a flat numeric damage bonus on a maintained weapon's next hit. The book-wide weapons rework (2026-08-19) forbids all flat damage riders in every location including ancestry gifts; a book-wide scan confirms this is the only surviving flat rider (every other damage-boost in the book uses the tier-bump wording). Expected: to reprice the rider one row up on the shared damage budget table. Violated convention: ZERO flat +N damage riders, book-wide. Defect 2 [04-ancestries-cultures:92]: the Halfling Lucky trait defines a boon as adding a bonus die to a 3d6 roll. Chapter 6's definition is roll 4d6 keep the highest three, and the brief states a boon is not an extra d6; the parenthetical must be deleted or reworded to the ch06 definition (ch02 line 236 repeats the Lucky trait but without the bad gloss, so only the ch04 line is in scope). Violated convention: Boon/Bane definition (ch06). Defect 3 (structural): all four gift tables (lines 148-193) carry only Gift/Tier/Effect and list no Discipline prerequisites anywhere, while line 144 promises the same card format as class abilities (whose tables include a Disc Req column, e.g. 05-classes:451) and ch08's ladder discipline (08-disciplines:109, 168) requires Adept cards to carry exactly 2 and Master cards exactly 3 prerequisites, always. Minimal fix: add a prerequisite column satisfying the ladder. Verified clean, for the disposition plan: no em/en dashes (0 occurrences); zero 'GM' occurrences (DA used throughout); all skill names in the culture tables match the ch07 roster exactly; all culture-table Disciplines exist in the ch08 taxonomy; the single cross-reference @sec-chapter-character-creation resolves (02-character-creation:1); no damage dice beyond sanctioned 3d6; 'Prone'/'Unconscious' are current ch13 conditions and 'short rest' is defined in ch21; gift counts are 5 per ancestry within the 4-5 bound with one Master each, consistent with the rarity guidance; Second Breakfast's 6 HP healing value sits on the Adept damage-budget row. The chapter is otherwise sound; the three named defects are the blockers.

evidence.claim: The Forge-Trained Adept gift grants a fixed numeric damage bonus on a weapon's next hit, a flat damage rider that the 2026-08-19 weapons rework banned book-wide, including in ancestry gifts; the canonical replacement is a one-row damage-tier bump.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: one maintained weapon deals +6 damage (flat) on its next hit

evidence.claim: The Halfling Lucky trait glosses a boon as an added die on a 3d6 roll, contradicting the core-resolution definition of a boon as rolling 4d6 and keeping the highest three; the brief explicitly rules that a boon is not an extra d6.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: add one boon (an extra d6) to any 3d6 roll

evidence.claim: The gifts' intro promises the same card format as class abilities, yet all four gift tables (lines 148-193) omit any Discipline prerequisite column, leaving Adept and Master gifts with no listed prereqs as the ladder discipline requires.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: They follow the same card format as class abilities

evidence.claim: Canon definition of Boon and Bane: roll four d6 and keep the highest three (lowest three for Bane), establishing the expected value for the Lucky trait fix.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: you roll 4d6 and keep the highest three

evidence.claim: Ladder canon from the discipline chapter: only basic Novice cards may be prerequisite-free, while Adept and Master cards always require Disciplines, so gift-table rows at those tiers without any listed prerequisite contradict it.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: These represent minor talents anyone can pick up

evidence.claim: Tier equals prerequisite count: Novice one, Adept two, Master three Disciplines, which is the exact shape a prerequisite column in the gift tables must satisfy.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Novice = 1, Adept = 2, Master = 3

evidence.claim: Checks verified clean on the chapter text: zero em/en dash characters and zero GM occurrences; every skill name in the culture tables matches the ch07 roster; every Discipline named exists in the ch08 taxonomy; the only cross-reference resolves to ch02 line 1; no damage dice beyond 3d6; gift counts 5 per ancestry within the 4-5 bound with one Master each; 6 HP healing value sits on the Adept budget row.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: scan results: emdash=0, GM=0, skills/disciplines all match rosters, 1 xref resolves

payload.argument: The Dwarf ancestry gift Forge-Trained at [04-ancestries-cultures:181] lets a maintained weapon add six flat points of damage on its next strike, once per scene. That is a flat +N damage rider, a form the weapons rework (2026-08-19, book-wide) declares dead anywhere in the book including ancestry gifts, and it is not a sanctioned damage-TIER bump. It also breaks the chapter's own ceiling rule at [04-ancestries-cultures:146]: a flat +6 on a Standard Adept hit (9) reaches 15, which exceeds the 12 cap every Adept-tier class ability is keyed to on the damage budget, and on a Strong hit (12) it reaches 18, past even the Master Adept-strong ceiling. A rules-lawyer dwarf simply out-damages the class they are supposed to complement, and the DA has no table to read, because the number is a rider off the table rather than a budget row. Violated conventions: the book-wide ban on flat +N damage riders, and the ceiling rule that a gift must never exceed the power of a class ability at the same tier. Minimal fix: delete the flat +6 and replace it with a sanctioned bump, e.g. 'once per scene, your next maintained-weapon attack deals damage one tier up on the damage budget'.

evidence.claim: The Adept gift Forge-Trained grants a flat +6 damage rider on a maintained weapon's next hit, a form the book-wide weapons rework banned and which the damage budget table does not sanction.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: one maintained weapon deals +6 damage (flat)

evidence.claim: The damage budget's Adept row caps Strong at 12, so any flat rider added on top of an Adept hit pushes a gift above the tier every Adept class ability is keyed to.

Worked counter-example: a dwarf with an Adept-tier axe deals 9 damage on a Standard roll (Adept row) and 12 on a Strong roll; with Forge-Trained's flat +6 those become 15 and 18 respectively, exceeding the 12 Adept Strong ceiling and out-performing every Adept class ability on the budget.

payload.argument: Refute: two verified convention breaks, everything else in the chapter verifies against canon. Primary (mechanical): [04-ancestries-cultures:181] prices the Dwarf Adept forge gift as a flat damage add-on to a weapon hit. That rider pattern was retired book-wide by the 2026-08-19 weapons rework and this is now the only remaining instance in the whole book; the arithmetic also lands off-budget (Adept Standard 9 plus 6 equals 15, which is not on the Adept 6/9/12 row), outperforming the canonical one-tier bump that same tier offers in ch05 and ch15. Violated convention: zero flat +N damage riders; every damaging number must be a budget row, a Basic-card floor, or a tier bump. Minimal fix: reprice the rider as one damage-tier row up on the damage budget. Secondary (vocabulary/definition): [04-ancestries-cultures:92] glosses the Halfling boon as an extra die, contradicting ch06's definition of a boon as four d6 keeping the highest three. Minimal fix: delete the parenthetical; the ch02 table (02:66) already states the trait without it. Verified clean, so the fix scope is exactly these two lines: ancestry and culture tables match ch02's creation tables row for row; every skill name resolves in the ch07 roster and every Discipline in the ch08 roster; @sec-chapter-character-creation resolves to ch02:1 and the Quick Study cross-reference resolves to ch09:185; five gifts per ancestry with a single Master (rare, as required); the 6 HP healing values sit on Adept budget rows; cost defers to ch02's flat 2/4/8 DP card pricing; zero em-dashes, no GM usage, no damage dice anywhere in the chapter. For the librarian: the ch21 glossary (21:27) carries the same stale boon gloss and may need a companion fix outside this source.

evidence.claim: The Dwarf Adept gift prices a flat damage add-on onto a maintained weapon hit, the exact phrasing the 2026-08-19 rework retired book-wide; this is the only surviving instance in the book.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: one maintained weapon deals +6 damage (flat)

evidence.claim: Applied to an Adept weapon, the rider pushes a Standard hit from its 9 row to 15, a value absent from the Adept 6/9/12 budget rows, exceeding the canonical one-tier boost.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: 9 (Adept Standard) + 6 (rider) = 15; Adept rows are 6/9/12

evidence.claim: Post-rework canon phrases any weapon damage boost as a one-row tier bump on the damage budget, not as a flat add-on.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: deals +1 damage tier, the row one step up

evidence.claim: The Halfling trait prose glosses a boon as an extra die, contradicting the ch06 definition.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: add one boon (an extra d6)

evidence.claim: Core resolution canon defines a boon as rolling four d6 and keeping the highest three, never as an added die.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: roll 4d6 and keep the highest three

evidence.claim: The chapter's ancestry and culture tables match ch02's creation tables row for row, and ch02 states the Lucky trait without the erroneous boon gloss.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Lucky: add one boon to any roll, once per session

payload.argument: The dwarf Adept gift Forge-Trained [04-ancestries-cultures:181] lets a maintained weapon deal +6 flat damage on its next hit. That is a fixed additive damage rider, which the book-wide weapons rework of 2026-08-19 abolished for every location, including ancestry gifts. It also fails the budget law: +6 is not a budget row (Adept is 6/9/12), not a Basic-card floor, and not a tier bump. Worked math: a +6 rider on Adept hits yields 12/15/18, which matches no row of the 2/4/6, 6/9/12, 9/15/21 ladder. The sanctioned mechanism for making a hit hit harder is one row up on the damage budget, as written for Charge Attack [15-equipment.qmd:193] and defined at the budget table [08-disciplines.qmd:172]. Minimal fix: replace the flat rider clause with 'the next hit deals one damage tier higher.' Everything else I checked passed: gift counts (3/4/3/4), Adept/Master prereq shapes (exactly 2 / exactly 3), flat 2/4/8 card costs [22-reference-sheets.qmd:242-247], L3/L7 gates, skill names against the ch07 roster, and cross-refs @sec-damage-budget [08-disciplines.qmd:172] and @sec-chapter-character-creation [02-character-creation.qmd:1].

evidence.claim: The dwarf Adept gift Forge-Trained gives a maintained weapon a flat +6 damage boost on its next hit, usable once per scene.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: deals +6 damage (flat) on its next hit

evidence.claim: The damage budget is the single balance spine of the book; every damaging effect keys to its flat rows and no separate damage roll exists.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: The table is the law.

evidence.claim: The canonical way to strengthen a hit moves it one row up on the budget rather than adding a fixed number of damage.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: your attack deals +1 damage tier

evidence.claim: Adding a flat +6 to Adept hits (6/9/12) yields 12/15/18, which is not a row of the 2/4/6, 6/9/12, 9/15/21 ladder, so the rider cannot be expressed as a sanctioned value.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21

payload.argument: The word 'boon' carries two different mechanics inside this chapter. The Halfling Lucky entry glosses the trait as adding a spare die to the base three-die roll [04-ancestries-cultures:92], but four gift entries in the same chapter use 'Boon' as the standard odds-shifting keyword [04-ancestries-cultures:166, 178, 179, 190], and the canonical definition in the core chapter is the four-dice keep-three-highest roll [06-core-resolution.qmd:45]. One name, two effects: a reader of line 92 gets a flat extra die summed into the total, while a reader of the gift tables gets a reshaped probability curve, and those are not the same number. This violates the locked Boon/Bane definition convention and splits the chapter's own vocabulary. Minimal fix: delete the parenthetical gloss from the Lucky trait line so the whole chapter means the same thing by 'boon', matching ch06. Secondary note, not part of this fix: 'Second Wind' also names both a ch06 bonus-roll result [06-core-resolution.qmd:145] and a Human gift [04-ancestries-cultures:157], a collision worth renaming in one place.

evidence.claim: The Halfling entry explains the Lucky trait by adding a spare die to the base roll, a description that conflicts with the book's formal boon mechanic.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: add one boon (an extra d6) to any 3d6 roll

evidence.claim: The core chapter defines a boon as rerolling with four dice and keeping the three highest, not as an added die on the original three.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: A Boon means you roll 4d6 and keep the highest three

evidence.claim: A gift in the same chapter uses Boon as the keyword in its formal sense, so the parenthetical on line 92 gives the word a second meaning inside one chapter.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: You have Boon on Perception checks involving sight

evidence.claim: Summing an extra six-sided die shifts a three-die total by a full point on average, while the keep-three-highest form is worth roughly two points but with no chance of a fumble; two readers could build two different expectations from one word.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: one name, two effects

payload.argument: Refute: the Halfling Lucky trait (04-ancestries-cultures:92) re-describes a boon as one additional six-sided die on a 3d6 roll, but the book's core resolution chapter (06-core-resolution:45) defines a boon as rolling four dice and keeping the three highest. The parenthetical teaches a mechanic the book has retired, so a reader who builds a halfling from chapter 4 alone will play the trait with the wrong procedure. This is a broken cross-reference in the chapter's own text, not a style nit. Minimal fix: delete the "(an extra d6)" clause at line 92, leaving the boon term to resolve to the ch06 definition.

evidence.claim: The Halfling Lucky trait parenthetically equates a boon with one extra six-sided die added to a 3d6 roll, once per session.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: add one boon (an extra d6) to any 3d6 roll

evidence.claim: The core chapter canonically defines a boon as rolling four dice and keeping the three highest results, not adding a die to an existing roll.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: roll 4d6 and keep the highest three

evidence.claim: Because chapter 4's own prose contradicts the book's single boon definition, a player who reads only this chapter would apply an incorrect roll procedure to the Lucky trait; the defect is broken, not merely incomplete.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: an extra d6

payload.argument: The mid-chapter visual break renders as a near-blank page. In the built PDF (page 67) a single 60%-width placeholder image and its caption sit alone on the page, pinned between two forced page breaks at source lines 96 and 102. This consumes a whole page and opens a whitespace gap that hurts scanning. Fix: drop one of the two page breaks flanking the figure (line 96 or line 102) so the image flows inline with the adjacent section, or anchor it to the Cultures heading so it shares a page with body text.

dissent.position: Refuted on the Forge-Trained rider (correct) but its 'gift counts 3/4/3/4' and 'Adept/Master prereq shapes verified' are counting artifacts - actual counts are 5/5/5/5 and the gift tables have no prereq column; the librarian's prereq-column defect 3 is the accurate statement. Orchestrator-corrected, not a position on the disposition.

payload.rationale: Topic t-01 closed 7-0 refute in round 1 (quorum 4, reject_quorum 4, no rebuttals), a terminal reject-majority: check returned action=recommend with no impasse, so no judge is required. All seven refutes name the same defect cluster: one flat damage rider (f-001 librarian, f-002 contrarian, f-003 researcher, f-004 game-architect), one stale boon gloss (f-001, f-003, f-005 author, f-006 editor-in-chief), one gift-table prereq gap (f-001), one name collision (f-005), and one near-blank render page (f-007 layout-expert). The orchestrator independently verified every defect against the named canon lines and the built PDF before this synthesis, and corrected two game-architect counting artifacts (gift counts 5/5/5/5, not 3/4/3/4; no prereq column exists). The disposition plan separates the four chapter-local mechanical fixes (shipped in one micro-PR this run, including the ch21:27 companion) from the single design-authority item (gift prerequisites), which is routed to decisions-pending for Bruce because it is a fork with no locked ruling and a materially different content footprint. No rulings were sealed (no impasse), so rulings_applied is empty.
payload.recommendation: Chapter 4 (Ancestries & Cultures) is REJECTED as a publishable unit, 7-0 unanimous, on a defect set the orchestrator re-verified against canon and the built PDF. TIER 1 (mechanical, same-day micro-PR, chapter-local + one cross-chapter companion): (1) 04-ancestries-cultures:181 - the Forge-Trained Dwarf Adept gift prices a flat +6 damage add-on to a maintained weapon hit; the only surviving flat damage rider in the whole book after the 2026-08-19 weapons rework, and off-budget (Adept Standard 9 + 6 = 15, not on the 6/9/12 row), so it also breaks the chapter's own ceiling rule (no gift out-performs a class ability at the same tier). Reprice as a one-row damage-tier bump, the sanctioned convention (cf. ch15:193 Charge Attack). (2) 04-ancestries-cultures:92 - the Halfling Lucky trait glosses a boon as 'an extra d6', contradicting ch06:45 (a boon = roll 4d6 keep highest three); delete the parenthetical. Companion cross-chapter: 21-glossary.qmd:27 carries the same stale 'An extra d6 added to a 3d6 roll' gloss and is self-contradicting on the same line (it also says 'Roll 4d6 and keep the highest three') - fix there too (mechanical, one line). (3) 04-ancestries-cultures:157 - the Human gift 'Second Wind' collides with the ch06:145 bonus-roll result 'Second Wind' (both 6-HP recovery); rename the gift to 'Second Breath' (verified 0 occurrences book-wide, so the rename is safe and single-file). (4) 04-ancestries-cultures:96/102 - the mid-chapter figure is pinned between two forced pagebreaks, rendering PDF p.67 as a near-blank page (figure + caption only); drop one flanking pagebreak so the image flows with adjacent text. TIER 2 (substantive): none. TIER 3 (design decision, to decisions-pending, NOT implemented): 04-ancestries-cultures:144 promises the gifts 'follow the same card format as class abilities', but all four gift tables (lines 148-193) are 3-column (Gift/Tier/Effect) with no Discipline-prerequisite column, while ch08:109/168 states Adept and Master cards always require Disciplines (tier = prereq count: 1/2/3). This is a genuine fork, not a mechanical defect: (A) gifts are exempt as innate bloodline traits (the chapter's own 'inherited, not learned' framing) and line 144's 'same card format' is an overstatement to be reworded; or (B) gifts carry discipline prerequisites and a 4th column plus ~20 new prereq assignments is owed - a content wave, not a micro-PR. No locked ruling covers gift prereqs, and the two directions are substantively different, so it goes to Bruce unimplemented. VERIFIED NOT findings (orchestrator re-check, per verify-before-trust): gift counts are 5 per ancestry (the game-architect's '3/4/3/4' is a counting artifact); the gift tables carry no prereq column (the game-architect's 'prereq shapes verified' is a false positive on that point - the librarian's defect 3 is the real one); every skill name in the culture tables resolves in the ch07 roster; every Discipline exists in the ch08 taxonomy; @sec-chapter-character-creation resolves (02:1); the Quick Study cross-ref resolves (09:185); Second Breakfast's 6-HP healing sits on the Adept budget row; 0 em-dashes, 0 damage dice, 'DA' used throughout (no GM); the ch02 ancestry table (02:66) states the Lucky trait without the bad gloss, corroborating the fix. The 7-0 is unanimous; the single dissent is the game-architect's two counting artifacts, which the orchestrator corrected against the file.

resolved.outcome: rejected (7-0, un-rebutted refutes, terminal reject-majority; no judge)
